name: Lattice
tagline: Live 3D capture of people from three old Kinect sensors, merged into one hologram you can view in a headset.
problem: Remote communication is still flat video; live 3D capture usually needs expensive studio equipment.
solution: Three Kinect v2 depth sensors, each on its own laptop, stream to a central server that synchronizes and merges them into one 3D point cloud at more than 20 frames per second; the reconstruction is viewed live on a HoloLens.
demo_moment: Team-described: a person standing among the sensors appears as a live hologram in the headset.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Selected by the organizer as one of 12 finalists among 261 submissions.
Worked around a one-sensor-per-PC SDK limit, interference between depth sensors, and a headset limited to an old Wi-Fi standard.
Pitched as the science-fiction hologram call, built from cheap discontinued hardware.
A finalist with no AI component at an event full of AI projects: hard real-time systems work stood out on its own.

lessons: In an AI-heavy field, a visibly hard non-AI build can be the differentiator.
